guideline: Manual error analysis of generated sentences focusing on three common mistake types: Syntax/Spelling mistakes, Lack of Information, Information Redundancy
Manual error analysis of generated sentences focusing on three common mistake types: Syntax/Spelling mistakes, Lack of Information, Information Redundancy
- We observed three common mistakes from the outputs: Syntax/Spelling Mistake, Lack of Information, Information Redundancy.
Annotators were asked to examine each generated sentence and identify whether it contained a Syntax/Spelling mistake, lacked information from the input graph, or exhibited information redundancy.

We observed three common mistakes from the outputs: • Syntax/Spelling Mistake: There are grammar mistakes or spelling mistakes. • Lack of Information: The information in the graph is not fully realised in the description. • Information Redundancy: Some information in the sentence is repeated.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated verbose guideline into a concise summary, kept the three evaluation criteria unchanged

overall_notes: The paper focuses on graph-to-text generation diversity with well-structured automatic and human evaluation. The human evaluation was limited to a small error analysis (5 graphs, 75 sentences) rather than comprehensive human judgment. The extracted metadata had some redundancy and implementation details that were cleaned up.
